item.title: 9/11 and "never forget" collide with the meme generation's dark humor
item.description:
America says "never forget" — but a growing share of Americans don't remember. Why it matters: More Americans are coming of age with no firsthand memory of 9/11 , creating emotional distance from the trauma and more room for dark humor and reinterpretation. The big picture: For Americans under 27, 9/11 arrived through textbooks, movies, social media and family stories rather than lived experience. That distance can make humor easier, amplified by algorithms that reward provocative content and a generational instinct to push back against mandatory reverence. By the numbers: About 83% of adults born before 2001 remember where they were or what they were doing when they heard about the attacks. But roughly 10% of U.S. adults were born after 2001 and have no firsthand memory of 9/11. That distance has allowed 9/11 to become fodder for a flood of memes, including ones using the iconic photo…
